brief.situation: You are the AVD administrator at Calder Engineering, a fictional design firm. The 60 engineers use personal desktops in the host pool hp-engineers; an automation deallocates them every night, and Start VM on Connect powers each one on when its owner connects. Yesterday the platform team moved the session host VMs from rg-avd-eng to a new resource group, rg-avd-eng-vms. This morning nobody's desktop starts. The client design review begins at 08:30.
handover: The platform team's move ticket lists the VMs, disks and NICs; nothing about role assignments.
Security policy: the AVD service principal gets only the roles AVD's documentation names.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the host pool, the session host VMs in their new resource group and the role that lets AVD start them.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the desktops did not start, what you assigned, and how a move keeps it working.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects the failed start to the scope.
parts.modelAnswer: The activity log showed AVD's start attempts failing authorization. Its Power On Contributor role was assigned on rg-avd-eng, and yesterday's move put the VMs in rg-avd-eng-vms, outside that scope.

parts.label: Assigned
parts.criteria: Documented role, smallest scope that works.
parts.modelAnswer: Desktop Virtualization Power On Contributor for the AVD service principal on rg-avd-eng-vms. Contributor on the subscription would also work but breaks least privilege.

parts.label: Moves
parts.modelAnswer: The assignment is in the AVD Bicep with the resource group, and the move runbook now re-creates assignments whose scope no longer contains the resources.

expertPath.text: Failed start/action with AuthorizationFailed; Power On role only on the old resource group; feature on; all VMs deallocated.

overPrivileged.headline: The right role at the right scope
overPrivileged.body: Start VM on Connect needs Desktop Virtualization Power On Contributor at a scope that contains the session hosts. A broader role works too, and breaks least privilege.

reviewWithout.headline: A role assignment does not follow a move
reviewWithout.body: A role assigned on a resource group covers what is in it. Move the VMs and the assignment no longer contains them.

starting.headline: Good: least privilege, right scope
starting.body: You read the failed start in the activity log, found the assignment on the old scope, assigned the documented role on the new one, checked a real connection, and fixed the move process.

scoring.modelReasoning: AVD tried to start the desktops and was refused authorization. Its Power On role is assigned on the resource group the VMs left yesterday, so the scope no longer contains them. Assign Desktop Virtualization Power On Contributor on the new resource group, check a real connection, and make role assignments part of moves. Contributor on the subscription is far more than the feature needs; toggling the feature changes nothing.
